newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-FULKE CHALLENGES LEHMAN WITH A 64.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FULKE CHALLENGES LEHMAN WITH A 64.

text.p: Unheralded Swede Pierre Fulke completed a seven-under-par 64 to challenge big-name Americans Tom Lehman and Steve Jones in the Loch Lomond World Invitational on Friday.
Fulke ran in five successive birdies on the back nine after resuming his weather-delayed second round at the 10th hole to move alongside Jones, three shots behind British Open champion Lehman.
The 26-year-old Swede, who has missed his last seven cuts and nine out of 11 events this year, would on his own in second place but for a bogey at the last hole.

But he will now play his third round with both Americans after the decision by officials to send out three-balls instead of the customary two-balls to get back on schedule after five hours were lost to electrical storms on Thursday.
Groups will also start from the first and 10th tees simultaneously.

Lehman, who defends his Open title at Royal Troon next week, finished off his round of 66 late on Thursday night after a five-hour delay in play and said he could not see his shots land on the last two holes.
Jones, last year's U.S. Open champion, fired a 65 earlier on Thursday before the interruption.
Fulke, who had a hole in one in the opening round, said he was as surprised as anyone to be playing so well in view of his recent poor record.
Considered one of the best young Swedes when he placed 23rd on the 1994 European Tour money list, he took third place in the 1995 French Open and then his game fell apart.
He does not know why. But after plunging to 84th on the money list that year and 93rd last year, he has engaged a new caddie this year to help him out.
"I haven't had much luck with coaches, maybe because I'm not a technical sort of player," he said. "So I'm using a new caddie and we have discussed a few things which seem to have helped."
First round leaders Joakim Haeggman of Sweden and Englishman Paul Curry shared fourth place another shot behind. Greg Norman and Englishman Stephen Field were five off the pace on six under par.
The halfway cut was confirmed at one over par and the casualties included Jose Maria Olazabal.
The Spaniard missed the cut for the first time in 11 events since he launched his comeback in February after 18 months away from the game with foot problems.
He lost out by one shot after a 74. Bernhard Langer of Germany, who won two successive European Tour events this year, missed his fourth cut in five events.
The woes continued for Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros who shot two 79s to miss his 10th cut in 12 events this year.
